mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (measured as the month-over-month change in FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower interest rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of declining FEDFUNDS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (UNRATE > 5.0) despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105) and payrolls (PAYEMS monthly change < 0) signals a weakening economic cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (INDPRO < 105 AND PAYEMS change < 0), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the early financial crisis regime (characterized by housing market distress and credit tightening), a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals persistent inflationary pressures that lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during the early financial crisis regime despite rising CPIAUCSL, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) from the previous month predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, as falling residential construction activity signals weakening consumer demand and economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below its 3-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (RSAFS < 3-month MA), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 210) and accommodative monetary policy (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) signals stagflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 210 AND FEDFUNDS < 4.5), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (marked by strong GDP growth), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during the late-cycle expansion regime when UNRATE rises, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
